from.place: Proof paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient adjunction and inverse-limit calculation; coherent diagram rectification foundation, via the products-of-Brown-localizations argument: Dual of Theorem 7.6.10, printed pp. 389-390, with the dual of App 1 and App 2 of Definition 7.6.1, printed pp. 386-387

title: Finite-colimit approximation criterion for infinity equivalence
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a common sufficiently large universe. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be quasicategories admitting all finite coherent colimits (diagrams indexed by simplicial sets with finitely many nondegenerate simplices), and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserve these colimits. Suppose $F$ is conservative, meaning an edge of $\mathcal C$ is an equivalence whenever its image is an equivalence. Suppose also that for every $x\in\mathcal C$, every $y\in\mathcal D$, and every edge $\psi:F(x)\to y$, there are $x'\in\mathcal C$, an edge $u:x\to x'$, and an equivalence $e:y\to F(x')$ such that $F(u)$ and $e\psi$ represent the same morphism in $h\mathcal D$. Here $h\mathcal D$ has morphism sets $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(-,-)$. Then $F$ is a functor equivalence, with a coherent quasi-inverse. No hypothesis that $F$ is fully faithful is imposed.

source.place: Dual of Theorem 7.6.10, printed pp. 389-390, with the dual of App 1 and App 2 of Definition 7.6.1, printed pp. 386-387. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Pass to opposites: put $A=\mathcal C^{op}$, $B=\mathcal D^{op}$ and $G=F^{op}$. Reversing the vertex order of each simplex defines the opposite simplicial set, reverses composition and exchanges coherent colimits with coherent limits; it preserves finiteness of the number of nondegenerate simplices. Thus $A,B$ have finite limits and $G$ preserves them and reflects equivalences. For an edge $\psi:b\to G(a)$, the hypothesis applied to its opposite gives $v:a'\to a$ in $A$ and an equivalence $e:b\to G(a')$ with $[\psi]=[G(v)e]$: take the inverse of the opposite of the equivalence in the hypothesis. An equality in the homotopy category is a path between the corresponding points of the Kan mapping space, so this assertion includes a chosen homotopy after choosing representatives. Call this the right approximation condition. It suffices to give a coherent quasi-inverse for $G$, because taking opposites of that inverse and its two natural equivalences gives one for $F$.

source.place: Definition 7.6.1 and Theorem 7.6.10; explicit passage from left approximation to right approximation

proof.text: For any functor $G:A\to B$ with the finite-limit, conservativity and right approximation hypotheses of step 1, fix $b\in B$ and let $P_b$ be the mapping-path homotopy fiber of $G^\simeq:A^\simeq\to B^\simeq$ over $b$. The cores are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], and $P_b$ is Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion]. Apply [lem-coef-finite-core-fiber-contraction]: $P_b$ is nonempty, and every map $K\to P_b$ with $K$ finite is simplicially homotopic to a constant map. Its hypotheses hold because the finite coherent limits and their preservation are exactly those established in step 1, and the approximation triangle has the orientation $[\psi]=[G(v)e]$. This includes the empty shape, using a terminal object. We now deduce weak contractibility from these finite-diagram contractions.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, specialized to equivalences and actual finite limits; expanded contraction of each homotopy fiber

proof.text: The finite-diagram contractions in step 2 make $P_b$ weakly contractible. Here are the required topological details. It is nonempty by the empty-diagram case. For any map $S^r\to|P_b|$, compact finite support [lem-cbc-realization-compact-finite-support] factors it through $|L|$ for a finite simplicial subset $L\subseteq P_b$. Apply step 2 to the inclusion $L\to P_b$. The realization-cylinder homeomorphism of [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] turns its simplicial homotopy into a continuous homotopy of $|L|\to|P_b|$ to a constant. Thus every such sphere map is freely nullhomotopic. For $r=0$ this joins any two points to one point, proving path connectedness. For $r\geq1$, regard a based sphere map as a cube map constant on its boundary, using $[0,1]^r/\partial[0,1]^r\cong S^r$. The basepoint-change formula of [lem-coef-homotopy-groups-basepoint-change] identifies its based homotopy class with transport of the constant class along the track of its basepoint; that transport is zero. Consequently all the based homotopy groups vanish. This proves weak contractibility under the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], including moving basepoints. The homotopy-fiber criterion [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] now shows that $G^\simeq$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Steps 2-3 proved this assertion uniformly for any functor satisfying step 1, without claiming full faithfulness.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.7, finite-test contraction; agent expansion using compact finite support and basepoint change

proof.text:
For $t\in A$ write $S_t=A_{/t}$ for the join slice of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Its $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\to A$ with final vertex $t$. It is equivalent over $A$ to the target-fixed arrow category $T_t$ by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence]. We will use its join presentation for finite limits. For a finite $K$ and $q:K\to S_t$, its simplices assemble to $\widehat q:K\star\Delta^0\to A$ with last vertex $t$, as in [lem-coef-join-slice-diagram-isomorphisms]. This shape is finite, including when $K$ is empty. The join cone category of $q$ in $S_t$ is degreewise isomorphic to the join cone category of $\widehat q$ in $A$: an $n$-simplex on either side is a map
$$\Delta^n\star K\star\Delta^0\longrightarrow A$$
restricting to $\widehat q$ on $K\star\Delta^0$. The identification respects all operators by associativity of ordered concatenation. The dual of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] identifies these join cone categories with the coherent comma cone categories and identifies terminal vertices with limiting cones. Choose a limit of $\widehat q$ in $A$. Its cone gives the corresponding terminal vertex on both sides, hence a limit of $q$ in $S_t$. Applying $G$ to that cone gives a limit of $G\widehat q$ by finite-limit preservation. The same degreewise identification and its naturality therefore show that the induced $G_t:S_t\to B_{/Gt}$ preserves finite limits. For $K=\varnothing$, $\widehat q$ is the single object $t$, so the resulting terminal object in $S_t$ is $1_t$; no assertion that the projection creates empty limits is used.

source.place: Corollary 7.3.29 as used in Theorem 7.6.10; agent explicit finite join-cone calculation

proof.text: The functor $G$ of step 1 reflects equivalences and has right approximation. Apply [lem-coef-right-approximation-slice] at $t$: the induced $G_t:S_t=A_{/t}\to B_{/Gt}$ is conservative and has right approximation, with equality in the slice homotopy category including its structural compatibility homotopy. This applies directly to the join slices used in step 4; no underlying-arrow equality is substituted for a slice equality. Together with finite-limit existence and preservation from step 4, these are all hypotheses needed to apply the uniform core argument of steps 2-3 to $G_t$.

source.place: Proposition 7.6.5 and Remark 7.6.6; explicit compatibility of the approximating triangle in the slice

proof.text:
Steps 4-5 verify every hypothesis of the intermediate assertion of steps 2-3 for $G_t$. Thus both horizontal arrows in the natural square
$$\begin{matrix}S_t^\simeq&\longrightarrow&(B_{/Gt})^\simeq\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ A^\simeq&\xrightarrow{G^\simeq}&B^\simeq\end{matrix}$$
are weak homotopy equivalences: the bottom one by steps 2-3 for $G$, and the top one by the same proved assertion for $G_t$. This use is uniform substitution in an already established assertion, not an application of the theorem being proved.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.10, proof: apply the core argument to the functor and all its slices

proof.text: For clarity, both vertical arrows in step 6 are Kan fibrations, and their ordinary fibers are the required mapping spaces. We check this uniformly for either pair $(E,z)=(A,t)$ or $(E,z)=(B,Gt)$. Put $p:E_{/z}\to E$. This is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], and its opposite $p^{op}$ is a left fibration, because reversing vertices exchanges the horn ranges $0<i\leq n$ and $0\leq i<n$, so the conservativity assertion of [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift] applied to $p^{op}$ makes $p$ conservative. It is also an isofibration in the sense of [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]. To lift an equivalence $h:p(s)\to a$, choose an inverse $h^{-1}$ and its triangle $h^{-1}h\simeq1_{p(s)}$. First lift $h^{-1}$ with target $s$ using the right $1$-horn lifting property, getting $s'\to s$ over $h^{-1}$. The right $2$-horn consisting of this edge and $1_s$, over the chosen triangle with vertices $p(s),a,p(s)$, fills to an edge $s\to s'$ projecting to the specified edge $h$. Conservativity makes this lift an equivalence. Inner-horn lifting is already part of the right-fibration condition. The core-fibration theorem now makes $p^\simeq$ a Kan fibration. Every simplex in its ordinary fiber over $x$ belongs to the core, since every edge projects to $1_x$ and conservativity makes it an equivalence. Hence its fiber at any $w\in E$ equals the entire fiber of $p$, namely the right-pinched $\operatorname{Map}_E(w,z)$ by the slice theorem. Substituting $(E,z,w)=(A,t,x)$ and $(B,Gt,Gx)$ gives the two claimed fibers. All identifications commute with $G$ because the slice projection and the restriction-to-initial-face formulas do.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.10, proof: mapping spaces as homotopy fibers of core slice projections; explicit isofibration check

proof.text:
For a Kan fibration of Kan complexes, the ordinary pullback over a vertex computes the homotopy pullback: in the replacement description of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] one may use the fibration itself, with its identity weak-equivalence replacement. Apply this to the two vertical arrows of step 6, at $x$ and $Gx$. The map of their homotopy pullbacks is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance]: the maps on total and base spaces are the two horizontal equivalences of step 6, and the remaining map is the identity of the point. Step 7 identifies the induced fiber map with
$$\operatorname{Map}_A(x,t)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_B(Gx,Gt).$$
Thus this actual mapping-space map is an equivalence for all $x,t$; in particular $G$ is fully faithful, including all higher homotopies.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.10, final comparison of the homotopy fibers

proof.text: Let $1_A$ be a terminal object. Its image is terminal because $G$ preserves the empty limit. For any $b\in B$ choose an edge $b\to G1_A$; right approximation supplies an equivalence $b\to G(a')$ for some $a'$. Thus the full essential image of $G$ is all of $B$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to the full faithfulness proved in step 8: its restricted functor is now $G$ itself, so it has a coherent quasi-inverse with both coherent natural equivalences. As explained in step 1, taking opposites gives the required coherent quasi-inverse for $F$.
